cards.explanation: The answer is that the time has not yet come. God says, “These people say, ‘The time has not yet come to rebuild the house of the LORD.’…” It's all about timing. I've said "I'll get to it later" so many times that "later" should have my mailing address.

The answer is living in paneled houses while His house lies in ruins. God asks, “Is it a time for you yourselves to live in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?” He puts their paneled houses right next to this house lying in ruins. That's the picture He points to, friends.
The answer is False. God says, “You have planted much but harvested little.” They did plant a lot, but the harvest was small.
The answer is False. God says, “You put on clothes but never get warm.” They put the clothes on, but they still don't get warm, friends.

The answer is that their money keeps slipping away from them. A bag pierced through has a hole in it, so whatever goes in doesn't stay. They keep earning wages, and the wages keep leaking out the bottom. It's like carrying a box of cookies with a tear in it and leaving a trail of crumbs all the way home.

The answer is so He may take pleasure in it and be glorified. God tells them to build the house “…so that I may take pleasure in it and be glorified, says the LORD.” The reason God gives is about Himself and His house. And He doesn't ask them to wait until the timing feels right first.

The answer is True, and God says it plainly: “And what you brought home, I blew away.” So the little they did bring home didn't stay either. It's like carrying a tray of fresh cookies in from the kitchen and having a gust of wind take half of them.

The answer is True. God says, “Therefore, on account of you the heavens have withheld their dew and the earth has withheld its crops.” The heavens withhold the dew, and the earth withholds its crops. Two things held back at once.
The answer is drought. God says, “I have summoned a drought on the fields and on the mountains…” Fields and mountains are both in it, friends.

The answer is False. God says He has summoned the drought “…on man and beast, and on all the labor of your hands.” The animals are named in it, not skipped over. So the drought doesn't spare them, friends.
